name: Danuri (Korea Pathfinder Lunar Orbiter)
short_status: Operating: in a 60 x 200 km frozen orbit since September 24, 2025, twice extended through December 2027 as of July 2026; a controlled lunar impact is planned for March 2028.
tagline: KARI · South Korea · Orbiter · 2022 · Commercial and multipolar Operating
stats: launch mass of South Korea's first spacecraft beyond Earth orbit

mission extensions, now funded through December 2027
in lunar orbit as of July 2026

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 4 August 2022 (August 5 in Korea), on a SpaceX Falcon 9 Block 5 from Cape Canaveral; 678 kg at launch, developed by KARI from 2016

facts.label: Lunar transfer
facts.value: A fuel-cheap 4.5-month ballistic lunar transfer saved about 165 m/s of delta-v over a direct route; the first lunar orbit insertion burn came on 16 December 2022 (UTC; December 17 KST)

facts.label: Lunar arrival
facts.value: Insertion took only three burns instead of the planned five; KARI confirmed on 28 December 2022 (KST) that Danuri was in its 100 km, 90-degree circular polar orbit, circling the Moon about every two hours

facts.label: Payloads
facts.value: Six: the LUTI high-resolution terrain imager (about 2.5 m per pixel), PolCam wide-angle polarimetric camera, KMAG magnetometer, KGRS gamma-ray spectrometer, a delay-tolerant networking (space internet) experiment, and NASA's ShadowCam

facts.label: ShadowCam
facts.value: NASA-funded, built by Malin Space Science Systems as a build-to-print copy of LRO's narrow angle camera telescope (founding PI Mark Robinson, Arizona State University); more than 200 times the NACs' sensitivity, 1.7 m per pixel from 100 km, imaging permanently shadowed regions by reflected light

facts.label: First extension
facts.value: Announced 27 June 2023: the cruise burned 172.92 kg of propellant against a 202.64 kg budget, and the roughly 30 kg margin stretched the mission from end-2023 to end-2025

facts.label: Second extension
facts.value: Approved by the Korea AeroSpace Administration (KASA) on 10 February 2025: mission runs through December 2027, with a 60 km low-orbit campaign, a frozen-orbit phase, landing-technology descent tests, and a controlled lunar impact in March 2028

facts.label: Frozen orbit
facts.value: Entered 24 September 2025: a 60 x 200 km elliptical orbit shaped by the Moon's lumpy gravity field that holds itself without propellant, planned to be flown through December 2027

facts.label: ShadowCam operations (new, May 2026)
facts.value: Intuitive Machines became prime contractor for ShadowCam operations on 18 May 2026 ($4.5 million cost-plus-fixed-fee over three years), in the same handover that moved LROC operations from Arizona State University to the company

facts.label: Still operating in 2026
facts.value: After a SpaceX Falcon 9 upper stage struck the Moon on 5 August 2026, NASA's Center for Near Earth Object Studies at JPL passed the predicted impact point to the Danuri team, whose LUTI camera imaged the new crater a few hours later and showed the prediction was accurate to about 1 km (0.6 miles); Danuri then sent coordinates that helped NASA's LRO team refine its own follow-up imaging (NASA, 18 August 2026)

facts.label: Site documentation role
facts.value: Danuri photographed India's Chandrayaan-3 lander at Shiv Shakti point with its high-resolution camera at 07:55 KST on 27 August 2023, from the 100 km orbit, four days after the landing

facts.label: PolCam
facts.value: The first instrument to conduct global polarimetric observations from lunar orbit; its calibration papers were still being published in July 2026

timeline: Lunar orbiter development begins at KARI, six years before launch
Named Danuri, a blend of the Korean words dal (Moon) and nuri (enjoy), after a national contest that drew more than 60,000 participants
Launched (August 5 in Korea) on a SpaceX Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral into a ballistic lunar transfer
The space-internet payload streams the BTS music video Dynamite to Earth from about 1.21 million km in delay-tolerant networking tests during the cruise

Lunar orbit insertion: the first burn on December 16 UTC (December 17 KST) starts capture, and Danuri needs only three of the five planned burns before KARI confirms the 100 km, 90-degree circular polar orbit on December 28 KST
LUTI returns black-and-white views of Earth over the lunar horizon, feeding site selection for a future Korean lander
NASA publishes ShadowCam's view of the permanently shadowed wall and floor of Shackleton crater beside LROC's near-black image of the same scene, a demonstration of its 200x sensitivity edge
ShadowCam photographs LRO as Danuri passes 18 km above it, the two orbiters closing at about 11,000 km/h
First extension announced: propellant saved on the cruise stretches the mission from end-2023 to end-2025
Danuri's high-resolution camera images India's Chandrayaan-3 lander at Shiv Shakti point, four days after its landing
LRO returns the favor, catching Danuri as a smeared streak on three successive orbits at 11,500 km/h relative speed
KASA approves a second extension through December 2027: a 60 km low-orbit campaign, then a frozen orbit, then descent tests toward a controlled impact
Seven months of low-altitude observations from 60 km, the closest sustained look of the mission
Enters a 60 x 200 km frozen orbit that needs almost no propellant to maintain, good through December 2027
NASA appoints Intuitive Machines prime contractor for ShadowCam operations ($4.5 million, three years) alongside its new LROC contract
After descent tests that simulate a landing approach, Danuri is slated for a controlled impact on the lunar surface
